title: Renewal Prioritization Matrix & Safety Net Playbook
body:
PURPOSE:
This is a working playbook for triaging renewal risk across mid- and high-touch accounts. It combines a concise prioritization matrix (score-based), a set of safety-net actions and tailored save plays, plus executive escalation triggers and templated outreach. Use this as the canonical short-form that CS managers can run during weekly renewal scrubs and QBR prep.

SCOPE & AUDIENCE:
- Primary: CSMs, CS managers, Renewal Ops
- Secondary: Solutions Eng (technical troubleshooting), Account Execs (commercial offers), Customer Success leadership (escalations)

QUICK START (two-minute triage):
1) Pull renewal list for the next 90 days.
2) For each account, compute the Risk Score (see scoring below).
3) Bucket into: Low (0–19), Medium (20–39), High (40–69), Critical (70+).
4) Apply safety-net actions per bucket (immediate actions in 24–72 hours).
5) For High/Critical, schedule Exec Escalation review within 48 hours.

RISK SCORING (weighted, simple to run in a sheet):
- Health Signals (0–30): product MAU change, feature adoption trends, support volume spike, quality regressions in evals
- Engagement (0–20): meeting cadence dropped, QBR no-shows, champion attrition
- Financial (0–15): contract size, % of ARR at risk, upcoming procurement deadlines
- Technical Risk (0–20): unresolved P1/P2s, private deployment issues, infra incidents impacting SLA
- Sentiment & Signals (0–15): NPS/CSAT trend, exec tone from emails, competitor mentions

Scoring example (one-line):
score = health_signals*1 + engagement*1 + financial*1 + technical*1 + sentiment*1
(subscores normalized to their max).

PRIORITIZATION MATRIX (actions by bucket):
- Low (0–19):
  - Owner: CSM standard cadence.
  - Actions: Confirm value metrics, add to automated QBR reminder flow, light health nudges.
  - Offer: No commercial concession.
  - Timeline: Standard renewal outreach.

- Medium (20–39):
  - Owner: CSM w/ manager oversight.
  - Actions: 30-minute "value refresh" call + one targeted success plan update. Surface small technical blockers to SE.
  - Offer: Small operational credits (up to 5% of period) or free enablement session.
  - Timeline: Outreach within 14 days.

- High (40–69):
  - Owner: CSM + AM + RevOps notified.
  - Actions: Deep-dive health review (60 min), run post-mortem for recent incidents, create remediation milestone plan with deadlines.
  - Offer: Structured commercial concession (discount, extended trial, or pilot extension) aligned with measurable milestones.
  - Timeline: Action within 72 hours; weekly checkpoints.

- Critical (70+):
  - Owner: CSM escalation to CS Manager + VP CS + AE
  - Actions: 1) Exec escalation meeting (30–45 min) within 48 hours. 2) Temporary technical escalation war-room (SRE/SE). 3) Draft formal remediation SLA and rollback/fallback options.
  - Offer: Customized win-back package (see offer templates) — requires VP approval.
  - Timeline: Immediate; daily updates until stabilized.

ESCALATION & ROLLOUT PLAYBOOK (who to ping, when):
- Trigger conditions (auto-escalate): Critical score >= 70; two consecutive severe incidents; public regulatory issue; legal procurement stop.
- Escalation path: CSM -> CS Manager -> VP CS -> CRO (if contract >$X) -> CTO/Head of Infra (if infra issue).
- Slack channel conventions: #cs-escalations (for high), #cs-critical (for critical) with subject tags. Use the template below for the escalation post.

Escalation post template (copy into Slack):
[ESCALATION] Account: {{account_name}} | Renewal: {{date}} | Score: {{score}}
One-line summary: {{primary_risk}}
Requested actions: 1) Exec triage call 2) Technical war-room 3) Commercial approval discussion
Owner: {{CSM}} | Time requested: {{iso_time}}

EXEC MEETING RUNBOOK (30–45 min):
1) 5 min — Current state and customer priority from CSM/AE.
2) 10 min — Customer voice (sentiment, executive emails, procurement notes).
3) 10 min — Impact and tech summary from SE/SRE.
4) 10 min — Proposed remediation + commercial path.
5) 5–10 min — Decisions & owners.

COMMERCIAL & OFFER GUIDELINES (safety-net table):
- Quick rules: No unilateral discount >10% from CSM. Anything above requires AM + RevOps sign-off.
- Common offers: operational credits, feature-based extension, time-limited discounts tied to milestones, professional services credits.
- Approval TTLs: Manager sign-off within 24 hours, VP sign-off within 48 hours for material concessions.

Sample offer language (email):
Subject: Proposal to secure continuity and value for {{account_name}}
Hi {{name}},
Thanks for the candid conversation earlier. Based on what we heard, we'd like to propose a targeted package to ensure you meet your launch milestones and preserve the value you get from Redwood:
- 2 months complimentary priority onboarding support (SE assigned)
- 10% operational credit on next invoice tied to 90-day milestones
- Monthly exec check-ins for 3 months
We believe this aligns incentives and buys time to deliver measurable outcomes. Happy to discuss on a quick call.
Best,
{{CSM}}

QBR CHECKLIST & TRACKER (copy into sheet):
Columns: account_name, renewal_date, current_score, bucket, last_touch_date, next_action_owner, next_action_due, offer, escalation_level, notes
Example row: "Acme Inc","2026-03-30","58","High","2026-02-05","Priya Rao","2026-02-10","pilot-extension","High - exec pending"

WIN-BACK & RECOVERY PLAYS (templates and when to use them):
- Recovery play A: "Operational Remediate + Proof" — tech-led, used when technical incidents cause churn talk. Timeline: 7–21 days. Deliverables: root-cause report, targeted patch, follow-up performance SLA.
- Recovery play B: "Value Re-sell" — Biz-led, used when customer lost sight of value. Timeline: 14–45 days. Deliverables: tailored workshop, success outcomes map, payment milestone.
- Recovery play C: "Executive Sponsor Swap" — leadership-driven, used for stalled renewals with exec apathy. Timeline: immediate scheduling; secure exec sponsor on both sides.

TEMPLATES (copy/paste):
- 1) Manager approval request (for >10% concession):
Subject: Approval needed — concession for {{account_name}} (renewal {{date}})
Body: CSM recommends a {{percent}} concession tied to milestones: {{milestones}}. Rationale: {{brief_rationale}}. Risk score: {{score}}. Requesting sign-off by {{date}}.
- 2) Customer-facing remediation summary (post-incident):
Title: Incident summary + next steps for {{account_name}}
Body: Incident timeline, root cause, mitigation steps taken, owners, expected impact, compensation (if applicable).

MEASURES / KPIs TO TRACK (dashboard):
- % renewals by bucket (Low/Med/High/Critical)
- Time-to-first-action for High/Critical (target <24–48h)
- Win-rate after intervention by play type
- Avg concession % by cohort
- Escalation-to-resolution time

NOTES TO SELF / OPEN ITEMS:
- We should formalize the score thresholds with RevOps and product (tag: CS-412).
- Need a small Airtable/template for capturing offers + approval audit trail.
- Verify legal constraints on credits for enterprise contracts >$500k (legal/finance check).
- Automate score calc from product telemetry: raise a ticket with infra telemetry team.

ADDITIONAL RESOURCES (links):
- Renewal guideline (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Renewal+Guidelines
- Previous save plays (examples): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CS/pages/2332/Save+Plays
- Jira ticket to automate scoring: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-412

NEXT STEPS (owner assignments):
- Priya: build starter sheet and a calculated column for score — due 2025-09-19.
- Ethan: draft the manager approval template in Salesforce/HubSpot — due 2025-09-22.
- Marcus: scope telemetry integration for health signals — due 2025-10-01.

--END--

(Internal informal notes: this is intentionally concise; aim for a one-page cheat sheet during live renewal scrubs. Keep a separate canonical doc in Confluence for long-form process and policy.)
